activities.anchor: For polymer chemistry the decisive groups are the ones that can open or condense
activities.caption: pair each handle pair with the mechanism it buys
activities.name: polyHandleMatch

config.prompt: The monomer alphabet — pair each handle with its mechanism:

pairs.right: opens and adds monomers forever — addition, no atoms wasted
condense, water out — the ester links of PET
condense, water out — the amide links of nylon
hydrogen bonding — and ethylene glycol, the condensation partner

config.why: Every plastic on a shop shelf descends from one of the two mechanisms — which is why the functional-group table is the most load-bearing page of the school organic chapter.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the name is the recipe
activities.name: polyNameCloze

config.text: 'Polyethylene terephthalate' tells a chemist instantly that the monomers are %%0%% and %%1%%, joined by ester links — hence recyclable by reversing esterification. 'Nylon 6,6' compresses further: two %%2%%-carbon monomers, diamine and diacid, alternating.
config.hint: One monomer carries two –OH; the other two –COOH; the short name counts each monomer's carbons.

activities.anchor: is secretly polymer chemistry's supply chain
activities.caption: trace the monomer supply chain
activities.name: polySupplyOrder

config.prompt: From crude oil to plastic — put the supply chain in order:
items: Crude oil is fractionally distilled into fractions
The light naphtha fraction is cracked — heated with steam or a zeolite catalyst
Big alkanes snap into small alkenes: decane → ethene + octane
Ethene feeds polyethylene, PVC (via chloroethene) and polystyrene (via ethylbenzene)
config.why: Carbon locked in a plastic bottle is carbon not immediately burned — which reframes recycling as carbon bookkeeping, not just waste management.

activities.anchor: One mechanism, five states of matter
activities.caption: which curve is the alkane boiling trend?
activities.name: polyBoilTrace

config.prompt: Dispersion forces accumulate with chain length. Which curve shows an alkane's boiling point against chain length?
config.why: Methane a gas at −162 °C, butane a gas at −1 °C, octane a liquid at 126 °C, candle wax a solid, polyethylene a tough solid melting near 130 °C — the same chain, one accumulating mechanism.

activities.caption: drag the divider — one polymer, two materials
activities.name: polyPeCompare

config.prompt: HDPE vs LDPE — drag the divider across the shelf:

before.label: high-density PE
before.text: Straight chains, packed, rigid — milk bottles. The chains crystallise because nothing interrupts the packing.

after.label: low-density PE
after.text: Branched, tangled, flexible — squeeze bags. The branches wreck the packing, so the material stays amorphous and soft.

config.why: Differing only in how the polymerisation was run — the same lesson as isotactic polypropylene packing into crystals while the atactic random version is a tacky wax.

activities.caption: one line of the nylon stoichiometry is wrong
activities.name: polyWaterSpot

config.prompt: One line of this nylon 6,6 stoichiometry is wrong. Find it.
lines: Nylon 6,6 condenses hexamethylenediamine with adipic acid — alternating amide links
Hydrogen bonding between chains makes a fibre that outperformed silk
Each amide link releases one water
Polymerising n diamine with n diacid liberates n water molecules
The equilibrium is the design constraint — condensation is reversible, which is why PET can be chemically recycled
config.correction: Polymerising n diamine with n diacid liberates 2n − 1 water molecules — an 18 g/mol tax per link that must be removed or the reaction stalls at oligomer.
config.why: End-groups count too: leave the water in and the reverse hydrolysis keeps undoing links — the same reversibility that makes PET chemically recyclable.

activities.caption: file each effect under its control knob
activities.name: polyKnobBuckets

config.prompt: Three knobs set a plastic's properties. File each effect:

items.label: straight regular chains pack: stiff, opaque, stronger
tangled coils stay amorphous, clear, soft

config.why: Two independent knobs — long straight chains can pack or long tangled coils can refuse to — and the mix decides wax, squeeze bag or milk bottle.

activities.anchor: is held together by intermolecular forces between chains
activities.caption: true or false — one molecule or many
activities.name: polyBagJudge

statements.s: Within one polyethylene chain, covalent bonds run thousands of carbons long — molecular weights of 100,000+ are ordinary.
statements.why: Within the chain, yes: the backbone is covalent end to end.

statements.s: The bag as a whole is held together by covalent bonds running between chains.
statements.why: Chains slide or tear past each other — you rarely break the backbone.

statements.s: Polyethylene melts rather than decomposing into monomers, so the melt can be remoulded — thermoplastic behaviour.
statements.why: Intermolecular forces are overcome, the backbone survives.

statements.s: Thermosets like Bakelite keep the remoulding ability.
statements.why: They deliberately give it up: one cross-linked network, no melting.
